html:
Agent and request lifecycle

Ingress, execution and observation

Start with the system flow map for the surrounding packages. The diagrams here describe the HTTP request boundary implemented by RequestRoutes. They distinguish three entry paths: a new request, a server-owned conversation task, and input for an existing run. Prepared requests capture accepted settings but do not start inference. The server task coordinator reserves attempts independently of the direct-request route.

Request validation and transient state explains the payload guards, local interaction projections and terminal-directory comparison that surround these paths.

flowchart TD Client[Browser or API client] --> New[New direct request] Client --> Prepare[Prepare request and capture settings] Prepare --> New Client --> Task[Conversation task admission] Task --> Queue[Server queue reserves an eligible attempt] Queue --> Submit[Internal new-run submission] New --> Submit Submit --> Preflight[Selected model and Gateway preflight] Preflight --> Bind[Bind capability and permission authority] Bind --> Claim[Check capacity and claim queued identity if present] Claim --> Worker[Publish request state and launch runtime worker] Client --> Reply[Reply or explicit approval for an existing run] Reply --> Input[Validate current checkpoint and commit input] Input --> Resume[Restore captured authority and resume same run] Resume --> Worker Worker --> Native[RuntimeHost and owned AgentLoop] Native --> State[Native state, receipts and trace publication] State --> Read[Summary, activity and SSE reads] Read --> Client

This is an ownership map, not one atomic transaction. Direct submissions can fail after a trace or conversation exists. Queued retries must preserve their original identity. The prepared-request guide explains claim replay; the conversation coordinator explains durable task admission, parameter holds and attempt reservations.

New request sequence

The sequence begins after unresolved parameter references have been handled. Browser-supplied context cannot supply resolved parameter contents, trusted Plan intent, capability ceilings or Gateway protocol facts. Internal queue callers can supply accepted snapshots through the explicit server-side arguments.

sequenceDiagram participant C as Caller or queue worker participant R as RequestRoutes participant P as Preflight and authorities participant S as Request and run stores participant W as Runtime worker C->>R: Submit prompt, target and accepted identity R->>R: Strip untrusted authority and resolve snapshots R->>S: Claim prepared trace or create request trace R->>P: Prepare selected model and Gateway alt Preflight fails P-->>R: Typed failure R->>S: Save failed trace with non-dispatch facts R->>R: Remove cancellation handle R-->>C: Error for this request identity else Preflight succeeds P-->>R: Model profile and target facts R->>P: Resolve capability ceiling and permissions R->>S: Create or validate conversation R->>R: Check available direct-request capacity opt Prepared queue submission R->>S: Atomically claim original queue binding end R->>S: Publish current-run and session context R->>W: Launch worker with cancellation handle R-->>C: Request, conversation, trace and stream URLs W->>W: Enter RuntimeHost and owned AgentLoop end Note over R,S: Trace, context and launch are separate boundaries Note over W: Worker launch is not proof of an external effect

Failures after preflight retain their actual submission stage. The route only attaches the explicit no_operation_authorized, executed = false and remote_effect_possible = false preflight facts when preflight has not completed. A claimed queued request without native or submitted-trace evidence is an unverified outcome; the claim does not authorize a fresh launch.

Human reply and approval sequence

Ordinary answers use human_input.accept_answer. The native transaction rechecks run status, Pause/Stop, interaction identity and duplicate input after the route's preliminary checks. A promoted Activity requires its current operation identity. Direct clients may omit that identity for legacy compatibility, but an identity they do supply must match.

sequenceDiagram participant U as User interface participant R as Reply route participant N as Native input transaction participant T as Trace and conversation presentation participant W as Resume worker U->>R: Answer with request and interaction identities R->>R: Check current wait and selected option R->>N: accept_answer with exact run scope alt Stale, duplicate, paused or stopping interaction N-->>R: InputConflict R-->>U: 409 conflict, no resume launched else Valid ordinary answer alt Promoted Activity N->>N: Append one activity_input wake event else Direct interaction N->>N: Stage clarification in unowned run checkpoint end N-->>R: Accepted state R->>T: Retain question and answer activity R->>T: Restore trace and publish running status R->>W: Resume original run with saved authority R-->>U: Same request identity and reconnect cursor W->>N: Acquire ownership and consume saved input W->>W: Continue ordinary decision loop end Note over N: RAM commit does not imply synchronous disk persistence

The diagram covers ordinary answers. Capability/resource decisions delegate to their authority owner and can return an authorized child run. Permission approval uses the separate confirmation endpoint: it verifies an unowned approval wait, accepts the exact grant, then resumes; denial requests cancellation. Unsafe-action approval has its own control. Reply text such as “yes” cannot replace those protocols. See checks and authority.

Reload and trace subscription sequence

Summary reads restore the answer and interaction controls without loading the complete execution history. Activity and raw model/command output have separate inspection endpoints. A legacy failed preparation can be settled into a failed trace during a read; that repair does not start execution.

sequenceDiagram participant B as Browser participant R as Trace routes participant T as Trace store participant H as Retained conversation history B->>R: GET request summary R->>T: Read compact presentation alt Presentation retained T-->>R: Answer, wait controls and timing else Trace presentation unavailable R->>H: Read summary-only retained turn H-->>R: Saved presentation or missing end R-->>B: Summary, or 404 when neither source exists opt Retained trace header exists B->>R: Open SSE with event cursor and generation loop Until drained status ends the subscription R->>T: Read coherent delta page T-->>R: Events, next cursor, generation and status opt Generation changed or reset required R-->>B: trace.cursor reset end R-->>B: Projected trace events opt No more events and trace remains subscribable R->>T: Wait for delta, up to 15 seconds T-->>R: Change signal or timeout opt Timeout R-->>B: Compact timing heartbeat end end end end Note over R,T: Read and replay do not run the model or execute tools

The stream stays open for pending, running, waiting_job and waiting_event. After other statuses it drains that page's events and closes; resumption returns a reconnect URL. A missing trace header is a 404 even when conversation history can still supply a summary. Generation resets rebuild event projection state so a cursor from an older trace cannot skip the replacement's events.

Model decisions and user-visible progress

For the internal reservation, provider-call and cancellation sequences, see model decisions, capacity and cancellation.

The API validates the request and attaches trusted gateway, conversation, credential and approval context. RuntimeHost.handle_request prepares the request; AgentLoop.run sends the current transcript and the currently advertised tool schemas to the model.

Request admission resolves the selected model before materializing the execution configuration. The run saves its resolved override map, profile, version and output reservation. Normal model decisions merge only explicit execution overrides; Provider Default fields stay absent from the provider request. Task Contract, recovery and summary calls retain their internal generation policies. See Model Configuration and saved inference identity.

Each accepted model call follows one sequence: validate envelope and arguments, check budget and scope, persist a dispatch claim, execute or perform a built-in control, persist the real result, append its observation to the same transcript, and ask the same model for the next decision. An invalid call returns an error observation for local correction. A dispatch whose external effect is unknown cannot be blindly replayed.

During native inference, the provider response arrives incrementally. smTO privately assembles content and native tool-call fragments, then applies the same complete-response validation. The existing trace SSE connection carries bounded, content-free receipt events to the status strip. “Thinking · receiving…” means provider data recently arrived; after three seconds without a receipt it returns to “Thinking…”. Tool activity starts only after a validated invocation begins.

The compact LLM stream activity waveform beneath that status shows when smTO receives streamed response data from the active model. Higher activity represents more stream events arriving within the display interval. A flat line means no model stream data was received during that interval. It does not represent model reasoning quality, GPU utilization, task completion percentage or hidden model thought.

The Timeline toggle beside Trace / Tokens/s shows or hides the Thinking and tool activity chips. The graph and timing totals remain visible, and activity continues to be recorded while the timeline is hidden. This preference is saved across reloads and browser sessions, and is also available as Show wavelet timeline under Settings → UI Preferences.

While a response is running, the elapsed timer shows time spent on that response. After completion, the conversation total appears separately and excludes time between responses.

Each completed response shows its elapsed time followed by tokens read | tokens generated, using totals across that request's model calls. These counts also appear in saved conversations with the wavelet or footer hidden. Provider counts take precedence; estimated counts use ≈, and unavailable counts use —. Generated tokens can include reasoning and tool-call output reported by the model. Each total also shows its average rate in tokens/s, computed as tokens divided by the summed model request time of finished calls with matching counts and timings. These averages exclude tool execution, idle time and in-flight calls, include stopped attempts with recorded usage and timing, and survive refresh and resume. Request time includes transport and prefill; these are observed request rates rather than GPU prefill or decode speeds. Estimated rates use ≈; missing timings show —.

Every validated native SSE data event counts, including private tool-call fragments, answer fragments and completion metadata. SSE comments, framing and the [DONE] sentinel do not count. Only timestamps and counts enter the graph payload; text, reasoning, tool names, arguments, credentials and partial JSON never do. Receipt counts use 100 ms buckets and travel in the existing llm.response.progress channel at most four times per second, plus a final flush. A pending timer flushes the last burst even if the provider becomes silent. No zero-only server events are needed.

The LLM stream activity graph is a continuously moving rolling timeline. It remains visible throughout the Agent session and shows actual model stream-data arrival as activity and silence as a zero baseline. One page-owned ring retains 600 samples (60 seconds at 100 ms per sample), refreshing at most ten times per second. New samples enter at the right; old history leaves at the left. The browser advances zero buckets during silence, including a disconnected trace stream. Background tabs suspend painting and catch up to wall-clock time when visible again.

The timeline synchronizes to the server's existing generated_at_ms timestamp at startup and when returning to the tab. It then advances using monotonic browser elapsed time. Receipt timestamps and “receiving” freshness use that same clock, so a different clock on a remote computer or phone cannot discard valid activity. CPU/GPU measurement values never enter the LLM graph.

The graph does not reset between model calls. Tool execution and waiting periods appear as flat sections because no LLM stream data is arriving. Completion leaves the recent trace visible; a new task shares the same history, including the idle gap. Only rolling-window expiry removes old activity. The compact status strip stays mounted, with “Ready” when idle and the current outcome after completion.

The height uses a rolling logarithmic count scale with a minimum visible height for a nonzero bucket; zero remains exactly zero. Cumulative counts replace earlier counts for the same call and interval, so replay cannot add duplicate spikes. Different calls in one interval contribute separately. Late receipts fill their original recent bucket. Available retained trace activity restores recent history on reload; no extra telemetry database or per-token persistence is used. The SVG is decorative, with one static accessible description and no sample announcements.

In Tokens/s, the color selector offers teal input / blue output or purple input / red output. The selected palette is saved for this browser tab, survives reloads and stays the same when the page switches between day and night themes. Both series use solid lines, matching translucent fills and a one-second rolling average, with separate Input and Output readouts. Output includes reasoning and tool output. The left axis scales input and the right axis scales output independently to their peaks over the visible minute, keeping both graphs legible when their rates differ greatly. Each axis is labeled and uses the color of its series.

Input prefers numerical provider telemetry. Live processing progress appears before output starts and preserves the reported batch intervals and pauses. Final processing durations can replace an earlier estimate, anchored at the first output receipt rather than response completion. That timestamp alignment still includes transport latency. Reported cached tokens are excluded from processing throughput. The input legend shows Measured, Est., or Mixed for the visible history; output arrival timing remains estimated, with its total count calibrated to final provider usage. Both curves are one-second averages: a subsecond burst can differ from the provider's average processing speed over its shorter active interval.

A third, solid amber line labeled ctx shows context remaining over the same minute on a fixed 0–100% scale, with no separate percentage axis. It uses the same latest recorded usage and output reservation as the context meter: it falls as the working context grows and can rise after compaction. Between usage updates it holds the last known percentage; unknown context stays blank. Switching conversations clears the plotted context history so values from different conversations are not connected.

The OpenAI-compatible adapter reads llama.cpp timings / prompt_progress, Groq usage.prompt_time (including streamed x_groq.usage), and Ollama evaluation diagnostics when a compatible gateway forwards them. Standard cached-token details and DeepSeek prompt_cache_hit_tokens are recognized. Only positively identified llama.cpp endpoints receive the optional live-progress flags; explicit setup rejections remove unsupported flags through the existing compatibility negotiation. Other endpoints need no extension to retain the fallback graph. This does not add a native Ollama or Anthropic protocol.

Without processing timings, reported or estimated uncached input tokens are spread over request transmission to first output, including reasoning. This remains labeled estimated: provider waiting and transport are not pure processing time. vLLM TTFT and aggregate server metrics are not relabeled as prompt-processing measurements. Native transport excludes tokenizer preparation and local slot waiting from this fallback interval. Missing usage retains the estimate; malformed optional diagnostics are ignored. Corrections replace the old call's entire interval, including zero-token corrections, and replay cannot duplicate or restore stale estimates. Calls with neither provider progress nor observed streamed output have no invented input-rate curve.

In Trace, prompt processing and generation pauses remain flat. Non-streaming fallback stays flat for the whole call, including its final complete response. The waveform also continues during safe answer streaming, and has no role in dispatch, completion, permissions, budgets, model configuration or timeout decisions.

The explicit completion control is finish_task: answered for information and requested source-code artifacts, completed for completed action/data work, or the existing incomplete statuses. No-tool answers need no evidence; tool-grounded answers cite real operation receipts. Code-only artifacts are not executed.

The final answer can appear progressively while the model generates it. Once the exact registered finish_task identity is established, a presentation-only extractor decodes its top-level message string. The existing trace SSE connection carries cumulative safe text through llm.response.delta; the status strip changes to “Generating…”. Plain assistant content can stream only for internal calls advertising no tools. The Agent always has finish_task; tool-enabled content stays private. Eligible terminal prose receives credential checks and ordinary completion/output validation through terminal_normalization.py; it can preserve a verified answer without a formatting-only model turn. Ambiguous work or unresolved presentation intent can still require explicit correction. Optional direct completion metadata on a capability call is validated after its durable result exists. Neither path fabricates an execution receipt. See completion normalization.

Every preview passes a credential holdback guard using the existing protected values and encoded variants before publication. Hidden reasoning, raw native arguments, completion status/evidence metadata and executable decisions remain private. The preview cannot authorize an operation or complete a task: the full native response, argument schema and completion evidence must still validate normally. Accepted final text replaces the same answer block. Rejection, cancellation or retry clears the preview; reconnect/reload restores cumulative text without restarting inference. Streaming follows the chat viewport only while the reader is near the bottom.

Streaming is automatic, with no preference or Behavior Effort setting. A provider that explicitly rejects compatible streaming before generation can fall back once to the ordinary transport, within the same reserved model decision. That capability result is cached for the client’s endpoint/model. A broken or incomplete stream stops the inference without a hidden retry. Model-call leases register a request-owned socket handle. Stop cancels that owner and interrupts its connected socket, including a blocked read; cancellation is also checked around connection and stream processing. DNS lookup may finish in its daemon worker after cancellation, but that worker cannot open a connection. Socket timeouts still bound uncancelled transport failures. See agent_turns.py and the shared cancellable_io.py transport owner.

finish_task carries the model's completion judgment. Deterministic checks reject missing or failed receipts, unfinished caller requirements, stale observations when current evidence is requested, and exact-value mismatches. They do not invent a new completion strategy.

ask_user, jobs, events, OAuth and budget pauses checkpoint the run. Resume continues that run with actual updates. Process waiting does not consume inference calls.

Whenever the model requires an ordinary reply to continue, it must call ask_user alone. A top-level decision mixing that control with sibling tools is rejected before any effect or receipt claim. Final communication uses finish_task; OAuth authorization and protected-action approvals use their protocol controls.

A pending ask_user pauses parent inference even when explicitly scheduled as an Activity. Already-declared independent graph branches and background jobs may progress under existing dependency, resource and approval rules. Dependent branches wait for the answer. The inline answer addresses the selected checkpoint once. The parent waiting_user status describes the inference checkpoint; it does not mean that every independent Activity has stopped.

If a user's reply determines the next action of this run, that question belongs in ask_user, not finish_task.message. Terminal messages must remain truthful and complete if the user never replies. Genuine external blockers and partial results may end declaratively; optional future suggestions and quoted questions remain valid. Before terminal acceptance, a narrow deterministic guard rejects explicit same-run continuation requests. The existing protocol recovery allows one correction to ask_user or a declarative finish_task, without replaying operations or consuming the completion-evidence retry budget. Rejected prose is removed from the answer view.

Removable destination choices use this same checkpoint. For supported USB/removable destination requests, unresolved targets consult current Gateway mount facts. An explicit user path uses ordinary path validation without an ambiguity scan; a selected volume binding retains identity revalidation. One eligible mount selects automatically; multiple eligible mounts require an inline reply before writing. Filesystem type, free space and enumeration order are not intent. The reply selects a persisted choice and the Gateway revalidates its mount/device identity before the next ordinary decision. Earlier artifacts and receipts remain intact. Missing or replaced destinations never cause a fallback to another drive. Current automatic OS discovery supports Linux; unsupported discovery returns unavailable rather than inventing a destination.

When the current run is waiting_user or awaiting_clarification, the main composer temporarily says Reply to me…. Send answers that run through /api/agent/clarification/<request_id>, preserving its task, Gateway, model and policy snapshots. The clarification card uses the same action. Replies are not reusable task drafts or queued prompts. Required choices use their option buttons. Authentication values use ordinary replies; OAuth browser/device authorization has protocol controls. Approval waits use explicit Approve/Deny controls. Typing “yes” in the composer does not grant approval.

Agent mode still creates independent ordinary tasks. Conversation mode still carries conversational context. Active interactions continue the exact run in either mode; answering a question never changes the selected mode.

The clarification projection includes the observed operation identity and, for a promoted Activity, its Activity identity. Both reply endpoints share native input validation within the native store's atomic transaction. The default Server uses the Controller RAM state hub; the retained standalone SQL store uses a SQLite writer transaction. Activity answers enter the existing activity_input wake journal before HTTP acceptance; owned resume appends the answer and its consumption marker in one checkpoint. It completes the Activity and clears waiting_activity_id before continuing. Generic clarification does not append it again. Direct answers retain their existing clarification context until consumption. Direct checkpoint writes reject while another owner is active so that accepted text cannot be overwritten. Duplicate, stopped, paused or replaced interactions reject without starting inference. Legacy direct clients may omit operation identity; current clients include it, and promoted Activity replies require it. Acceptance commits to the active state authority before returning; on the default RAM runtime this does not mean a synchronous disk checkpoint. Recovery after process loss depends on the saved generation described in state and recovery. The shared input boundary is human_input.accept_answer.

Reload reconstructs the same question from native state. Restart before input leaves inference paused; restart after input acceptance consumes the persisted answer. Manual Pause retains the interaction and defers consumption until Resume. Background job completion reconciles receipts while the human wait remains active. No schema migration is needed: existing checkpoints, contexts and wake events own these transitions. Outside an interaction wait, the server-owned task queue and captured task configuration remain in use. Its admission rules determine which tasks can run.

Conversation and Advisory modes share history. Advisory exposes informational controls and cannot execute external tools. Agent mode uses the full authorized tool loop. The canonical execution mode ID is agent.

Authentication questions and replies

ask_user uses one ordinary question and one reply for all missing information, including usernames, passwords, tokens and client secrets. Ask for related values together. The unchanged reply reaches the next normal Agent decision, which supplies literal tool arguments. No helper inference, parser, password vault or hidden retry is involved. An actual missing/rejected credential result remains an ordinary tool result; it does not create a separate wait. OAuth browser/device authorization uses waiting_user with oauth_authorization_request. Current OAuth expiry recovery lives in native/http_session_state.py; pre-baseline credential-wait records are unsupported.

Accepted monitoring snapshot

The global disabled_agent_check_monitoring_enabled preference is captured alongside the existing guard policy when a request, queued submission, conversation task or event is accepted. Request-owned prepared policy storage prevents a later Settings edit from changing accepted work. Public model/tool arguments cannot supply this authority. Native initialization, resume and continuation use the saved value; missing legacy values resolve OFF.

The snapshot only enables local diagnostic assessment of disabled checks. It does not add model turns, change the accepted tool catalog or trigger a scan/replay when Settings changes.

Accepted Activity supervision and attention

Global and conversation supervision settings are captured at acceptance for requests, prepared/queued submissions, tasks and scheduled events. Continuation and restart carry the accepted snapshot. Later Settings edits affect future acceptance. Older runs and prepared submissions receive the product defaults once; model arguments cannot supply watchdog authority. The settings surface provides enablement, healthy cadence and the attention threshold; the API validates the complete ordered policy. Health settings never control the runtime-owned completion clock. Short managed commands return to their attached Agent turn; only genuinely detached work uses continuation and health attention.

An observation worker can persist physical evidence and attention while the parent Agent is running or waiting. It never mutates an in-flight model request. At the next safe decision boundary, attention joins the existing continuation context. After the normal Agent-turn lease is acquired, dispatch rechecks Stop, completion and recovery. An attention-only continuation that no longer needs judgment returns to its durable wait without calling the model. Acceptance of the decision consumes only matching attention generations in the fenced checkpoint transaction.

An attention wake from a machine wait creates a durable, versioned recovery episode. It retains the original predicate, selected identities, absolute deadline, resume note, and run/epoch/amendment identity. Acknowledgement does not erase that wait. The episode allows three decision attempts, including rejected decisions, decision-loop retries and cached proposals; the allowance is saved before dispatch and included in model context. Transport retries and existing permission, batch and execution limits keep their owners.

After reconciliation, cleared faults or exhausted allowances restore the saved wait without another model call. Accepted recovery operations retain their identities and receipts; pending operations continue under normal activity tracking. Completion and expired deadlines are evaluated before attention and before restoration, using the normal wake/receipt path. Restoration never restarts a timeout. Explicit replacement waits supersede the saved predicate. User intervention, human checkpoints, Pause, Stop and terminal states retain precedence. Running tasks receiving attention do not acquire an artificial wait. SQLite and memory-backed stores use the same fenced lifecycle; restart cannot replenish attempts. Legacy silence-only alarms are suppressed, and an old resume note alone is never used to reconstruct a wait.

These bounds do not depend on optional repeated-read or no-progress guards, shell command similarity, or prompt caching.

Terminal jobs continue through the existing receipt and completion mailbox. Attention is nonterminal and does not create another completion channel. Human input, user amendments, Stop and existing completion delivery retain their precedence.
